語音辨識常把人名、公司、產品、術語聽成同音字。這個庫把確定的更正記在 `{fil:
Speech recognition often turns names, companies, products and terms into similar-sounding words. This knowledge base records confirmed corrections in `{file}`; after each ingest round wiki-feeder hands it to the phone app, so later meeting drafts use the right spelling.

- **When the user points out that a meeting page got something wrong** (for example "on the 10/21 sales weekly page, 'Jon Smyth' should be 'Jon Smith'"): fix the page **and record the correction in this table** (add a row, or add to an existing row). Only record what speech recognition misheard; plain typos and corrections to the content itself are not recorded
- Read this table before ingesting a transcript and write the correct spellings on the pages; if you are sure something was misheard while ingesting, record it too
- Format: the first line is `# Name corrections`, followed by a table `| Misheard | Correct | Group |`; one row per correct spelling, several misheard spellings separated by commas
- Group: if it is only misheard in one meeting series and replacing it elsewhere would be wrong, put that series name (the phone applies it to meetings whose title contains it); leave it empty if it applies to every meeting.
  **Two-character Chinese words only take effect when a group is filled in**
- Don't record anything you are not sure of; if the correct spelling is still uncertain, add `?` after it (it will not be applied). Only delete a row when the user says the replacement was wrong
請根據 Andrej Karpathy 的 LLM Wiki 設計模式,在這個資:
Following Andrej Karpathy's LLM Wiki design pattern, please set up a personal knowledge base system in this folder.
- The source material is in {raw} (I put files there; you only read, never modify). Its subfolder {pending}\ (keep this exact folder name, do not rename or translate it) is the single entry point:
  every new file I drop goes into {pending}\ first. Before ingesting, decide where the content belongs and mv the file into
  the matching topic subfolder under {raw} (subfolder names match the groups in Wiki_Pages\), then start writing pages. The source path cited on a page is
  the location after the move, and {pending}\ must be empty once ingestion is done. Write this triage workflow explicitly into CLAUDE.md
- Binary files in {raw}{pending}\ (PDF, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, scans, images, emails, audio/video recordings)
  are converted to Markdown first by another program (wiki-feeder), which tells you at ingest time where the converted file is;
  only when it says there is no transcription do you read the original directly. Don't install or run any conversion tool yourself,
  and never write converted files back into {raw}. Write this rule into CLAUDE.md too
- Wiki_Pages\ holds the Markdown notes you compile, including an index.md table of contents
- Write a CLAUDE.md at the root that defines your role (knowledge compiler), the ingest/query/health-check workflows, and quality standards for English and Markdown
- Write CLAUDE.md and every page in English
- I don't use Obsidian. All links between pages (including index.md) must be standard Markdown links [name](path.md);
  Obsidian's wikilink syntax [[name]] is forbidden. Write this rule explicitly into the quality standards in CLAUDE.md

The version history of this folder is managed with git by wiki-feeder: on the first automatic ingest it runs `git init`, makes one commit per ingest,
and keeps a backup in its state folder. Files dropped into the inbox from an iPhone are transcribed automatically by wiki-feeder, placed in `{pending}` (pending) in the originals folder, and ingested according to this file.

- **Never run git yourself** (no init, add, commit, push, reset, checkout or stash), and don't touch `.git/`:
  wiki-feeder only accepts commits it has verified itself; one extra commit from anyone else stops automatic ingestion until a person sorts it out
- Pages edited by hand just need to be saved, not committed: before the next automatic ingest, wiki-feeder saves them as a "manual edit snapshot" commit
- Commit message format for automatic ingests: `Ingest: <original file name> — one-line summary`; the body lists the pages added or expanded this time
- To see a page's history or restore an earlier version: tell the user to ask the person who installed wiki-feeder for them; don't touch git yourself
